item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Mary left Apton and rode at the same speed for 2 hours.

She reached this sign.

[Image: a girl on a bike facing right side stopping in front of a sign. The sign is written with “Brandon, 45 km” with a right arrow and “Apton, 30 km” with a left arrow.]

Mary continues to ride at the same speed to Brandon.

How many hours will it take her to ride from the sign to Brandon?
item.figure_description: A silhouette of a girl on a bicycle facing right, stopped beside a rectangular road sign mounted on a post. The top section of the sign displays the text "Brandon, 45 km" followed by a right-pointing arrow (►). The bottom section displays a left-pointing arrow (◄) followed by the text "Apton, 30 km".

A pie chart showing how Mary spent her time one day, divided into five labeled sectors:
- "Homework 10%": from the 12 o'clock vertical radius clockwise to roughly 1 o'clock.
- "Sleeping & Resting 40%": from roughly 1 o'clock clockwise to the 6 o'clock vertical radius.
- "Going to School 25%": from the 6 o'clock vertical radius clockwise to the 9 o'clock horizontal radius.
- "Eating 10%": from the 9 o'clock horizontal radius clockwise to roughly 10 o'clock.
- "Playing 15%": from roughly 10 o'clock clockwise to the 12 o'clock vertical radius.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
